# Egami.Fonts: guide for coding agents

Egami.Fonts reads fonts and lays out text in managed code: TrueType, OpenType (CFF), WOFF, WOFF2, variable and color fonts,
OpenType shaping, bidi, font fallback and paragraph layout with wrapping, alignment and hit testing. Egami.Drawing's canvases draw
the result.

Namespaces: `Egami.Fonts` (typefaces, fonts, collections, shaping), `Egami.Fonts.Layout` (paragraphs), with `Egami.Drawing` to
draw.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `Typeface.FromFile`, `Typeface.FromMemory`: one face of a font file; `FontLoader.Probe` reads what a file holds.
- `new Font(typeface, size)`: a face at a size in pixels; `font.MeasureText(text)` gives its advance, ascent and height.
- `FontCollection`: faces by family; `AddSystemFonts()` adds the installed fonts, `Match(family, style)` picks a face.
- `canvas.DrawText(text, baseline, font, paint)`: one line, from Egami.Drawing.
- `Paragraph.Create(text, ParagraphStyle)` and `paragraph.Layout(width)`: wrapped lines; `canvas.DrawText(text, rect, style)` and
  `canvas.DrawTextLayout` draw them.
- `TextShaper.Shape(text, font, ShapingOptions)`: shaped runs with bidi and fallback, for your own layout.
- Egami.Fonts.Substitutes: bundled metric-compatible stand-ins for Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Calibri and Cambria.

## Samples

Load a font:

```csharp
// One face from a file; a collection takes an index. The bytes are read once and every table is parsed when first needed.
Typeface face = Typeface.FromFile(FontFile);
Console.WriteLine($"{face.FamilyName} {face.SubfamilyName}, {face.GlyphCount} glyphs, {face.UnitsPerEm} units per em");

// What a file holds, from its header alone.
FontProbe probe = FontLoader.Probe(File.ReadAllBytes(FontFile));
Console.WriteLine($"{probe.Kind}, {probe.FaceCount} face(s), {probe.Outlines} outlines");

// Damaged fonts load leniently with diagnostics; Strict throws instead.
var seen = new List<EgamiDiagnostic>();
var options = new FontLoadOptions { Context = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = seen.Add } };
Typeface lenient = Typeface.FromMemory(File.ReadAllBytes(FontFile), 0, options);
```

A caption on a photo:

```csharp
// A caption on a photo: white text with a dark shadow, its baseline 24 pixels above the bottom.
using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Create(640, 360, new Rgba8(90, 120, 160, 255));
var font = new Font(Typeface.FromFile(FontFile), 28);
using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = photo.CreateCanvas())
{
    var origin = new Vector2(24, photo.Height - 24);
    canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin + new Vector2(2, 2), font, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 160));
    canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin, font, Rgba8.White);
}
```

Measure text to fit a box:

```csharp
// A label shrunk until it fits a 200-pixel button, then centred on it.
const string label = "Download the full report";
var box = new RectF(20, 20, 200, 40);
var font = new Font(face, 24);
while (font.MeasureText(label).Advance > box.Width - 16 && font.Size > 8)
{
    font = new Font(face, font.Size - 1);
}

TextMeasure size = font.MeasureText(label);
var origin = new Vector2(
    box.X + ((box.Width - size.Advance) / 2),
    box.Y + ((box.Height - size.Height) / 2) + size.Ascent);
using Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create(240, 80, Rgba8.White);
using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas())
{
    canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(box, 8), new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255));
    canvas.DrawText(label, origin, font, Rgba8.White);
}
```

Paragraphs at any width:

```csharp
ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 16 } };
Paragraph paragraph = Paragraph.Create("A paragraph is shaped once and laid out at any width.", style);

// Each width gives an immutable layout: lines of glyph runs, positioned from the box's top-left corner.
TextLayout narrow = paragraph.Layout(120);
TextLayout wide = paragraph.Layout(400);
foreach (TextLine line in narrow.Lines)
{
    string text = paragraph.Text[line.Start..line.End];   // the line's text, its trailing space included
    float baseline = line.Baseline;                        // y of the baseline
    foreach (LayoutRun run in line.Runs)
    {
        GlyphRun? glyphs = run.Glyphs;                     // glyphs at their layout positions
    }
}

// No wrapping: the box is as wide as the longest line.
TextLayout unbounded = paragraph.Layout(float.PositiveInfinity);
```

Drawing paragraphs:

```csharp
ParagraphStyle style = new()
{
    DefaultStyle = new TextStyle
    {
        FontFamilies = [family],
        Size = 18,
        Color = new Rgba8(30, 30, 60, 255),
        Shadows = [new TextShadow(new System.Numerics.Vector2(1, 1), 2, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 80))],
    },
    Align = TextAlign.Justify,
};

// One call: wrap into a box, centred across the lines.
TextLayout boxed = canvas.DrawText("Paragraphs wrap, justify and drop shadows.", new RectF(10, 10, 300, 80), style, VerticalAlign.Center);

// Or lay out once and draw where needed, skipping lines outside the visible part.
TextLayout layout = Paragraph.Create("Laid out once, drawn many times.", style).Layout(300);
canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(10, 110), visibleRect: new RectF(0, 0, 320, 200));

// Inline placeholders (an icon, a badge) are drawn by a painter called with each one's box.
canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(10, 130), placeholderPainter: (c, index, box) => c.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(box, 3), new Rgba8(200, 60, 40, 255)));

// The same text as one path: glyphs and decorations.
Egami.Drawing.Path outline = layout.ToPath(new System.Numerics.Vector2(10, 150));
```

Mixed scripts with fallback fonts:

```csharp
// Whole text: lines at hard breaks, bidi levels, script runs, fallback fonts, runs in display order.
var font = new Font(face, 24);
var options = new ShapingOptions { Fallback = new FontFallback(fonts.Families) };
ShapedText shaped = TextShaper.Shape("Shalom: \u05E9\u05DC\u05D5\u05DD!", font, options);

float x = 0;
foreach (ShapedRun run in shaped.Lines[0].Runs)
{
    GlyphRun glyphs = run.ToGlyphRun(new System.Numerics.Vector2(x, 0), shaped.Text); // what a canvas draws
    x += run.Advance;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- Passing the top of the text to `DrawText(text, point, font, paint)`. The point is the start of the baseline; add
  `MeasureText(...).Ascent` to place text by its top. Paragraph layouts are placed by their top-left corner instead.
- Expecting a font file name or family name to work where a `Font` is wanted: load a `Typeface` first, or match one in a
  `FontCollection`.
- Assuming the installed fonts exist on servers and in containers. Linux images often have none: ship the font files, or use
  Egami.Fonts.Substitutes.
- Drawing text in scripts the font lacks (Arabic, Hebrew, CJK, emoji) without fallback. Give `ShapingOptions.Fallback` or the
  paragraph style's `FontFamilies` more than one family.
- Reloading the same font file for every call. A `Typeface` is meant to be loaded once and shared.
